corrected_complete_triples.relationship: Children dashed in judgment against Babylon
corrected_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm’s violent blessing concerning Babylon’s infants corresponds to Isaiah’s Babylon oracle describing their children dashed before them. Isaiah does not specify the psalm’s rock.

source_unit.text: Happy is the one who will seize your infants and dash them against the rock.

target_units.text: They will dash their children before them, plunder their houses and take possession of their wives.
Behold, I am rousing the Medes against you, who do not value silver or have need of gold.
They will shatter young men’s arrows and certainly not pity your children; their eyes will not spare the children.
Babylon, which is called glorious by the king of the Chaldeans, will be as when God overturned Sodom and Gomorrah.

corrected_complete_triples.relationship: Preservation amid affliction and hostile power
corrected_complete_triples.rationale: Psalm 137 anticipates being kept alive if the speaker walks amid affliction and recalls God stretching His hand against the enemies’ anger and saving him with His right hand. Psalm 17 recalls enemies overtaking him on the day of affliction and the Lord becoming his support and bringing him into a spacious place; it also expresses future assurances of rescue. The conditional expectation and remembered acts remain distinct; the right-hand image belongs to Psalm 137.

source_unit.text: If I walk amid affliction, Thou wilt keep me alive; against my enemies’ anger Thou didst stretch out Thy hand, and Thy right hand saved me.

target_units.text: He will rescue me from my powerful enemies and from those who hate me, for they grew stronger than I.
They overtook me in the day of my affliction, and the Lord became my support,
and He brought me out into a spacious place. He will rescue me because He desired me. He will rescue me from my powerful enemies and from those who hate me.

corrected_complete_triples.rationale: Both passages combine divine holding and guidance. Psalm 138 says God’s right hand will hold the speaker; Psalm 72 says God grasped the speaker’s right hand and guided him in counsel.

source_unit.text: indeed, even there Thy hand will guide me, and Thy right hand will hold me fast.

target_units.text: And I am continually with Thee; Thou didst grasp my right hand.
In Thy counsel Thou didst guide me, and with glory Thou didst receive me.

corrected_complete_triples.relationship: Goliath’s challenge in the named heading
corrected_complete_triples.rationale: The source heading explicitly concerns Goliath; the account in 1 Samuel names Goliath and records his challenge to Israel for single combat. This identifies the named narrative figure without requiring every poetic battle image to be a literal detail of the encounter.

source_unit.text: Of David, concerning Goliath. Blessed is the Lord, my God, who trains my hands for battle array, my fingers for war.

target_units.text: A mighty man came out from the foreigners’ battle line, named Goliath, from Gath. His height was four cubits and a span.
A helmet was on his head, and he wore a coat of chain armour. His armour’s weight was five thousand shekels of bronze and iron.
Bronze greaves were on his legs, and a bronze shield was between his shoulders.
His spear’s shaft was like a weavers’ beam, and its iron head weighed six hundred shekels. The one carrying his weapons walked before him.

He stood and shouted to Israel’s battle line, “Why have you come out to draw up for war opposite us? Am I not a foreigner, and are you not Saul’s Hebrews? Choose a man for yourselves and let him come down to me.
If he can fight me and strike me down, we will become your slaves. But if I prevail and strike him down, you will become our slaves and serve us.”
The foreigner said, “Behold, I have defied Israel’s battle line today, on this day. Give me a man, and let the two of us fight in single combat.”

corrected_complete_triples.relationship: Speaking of fearsome works and divine power
corrected_complete_triples.rationale: Psalm 144 anticipates speech about the power of God’s fearsome acts and His greatness. Psalm 65 commands speech to God calling His works fearsome, then says His enemies will lie to Him through the abundance of His power. The fearsome-works and power language is shared, while the target’s consequence for enemies is distinct.

source_unit.text: They will speak of the power of Thy fearsome acts, and they will recount Thy greatness.

target_units.text: Say to God, “How fearsome are Thy works! Through the abundance of Thy power, Thine enemies will lie unto Thee.

corrected_complete_triples.relationship: A praise summons with differing goodness clauses
corrected_complete_triples.rationale: Both summon praise of the Lord and follow it with a goodness clause. Psalm 146 calls a psalm good and asks that praise please God; Psalm 134 calls the Lord good and commands music to His name, adding “for it is beautiful.” The repeated form is compared without equating the subjects of good or resolving the final it.

source_unit.text: Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah. Praise the Lord, for a psalm is good; may praise be pleasing to our God.

target_units.text: Praise the Lord, for the Lord is good; make music to His name, for it is beautiful.

corrected_complete_triples.relationship: Divine breath or wind controls frost and water
corrected_complete_triples.rationale: Psalm 147 says God will send His word and melt them, blow His wind, and waters will flow. Elihu says frost will be given from the Strong One’s breath and He steers water as He wishes. Divine wind or breath and control of water connect the passages, while frost-giving and melting remain different actions.

source_unit.text: He will send His word and melt them; He will blow His wind, and waters will flow.

target_units.text: From the Strong One’s breath frost will be given, and He steers the water however He wishes.

corrected_complete_triples.relationship: Creation endures under God’s established word
corrected_complete_triples.rationale: The enduring establishment and command that will not pass away correspond to God’s word remaining in heaven, the founded earth remaining, and the day remaining by His arrangement. The exact subjects and time expressions remain distinct.

source_unit.text: He established them for the age and for the age of the age; He set a command, and it will not pass away.

target_units.text: Twelve: Labd. For ever, Lord, Thy word remains in heaven.
Thy truth is from generation to generation; Thou didst found the earth, and it remains.
By Thine arrangement the day remains, for all things are Thy servants.

corrected_complete_triples.relationship: Praise in heavenly and holy assembly language
corrected_complete_triples.rationale: Praise among God’s holy ones and in the firmament of His power corresponds to the heavens acknowledging His wonders and His truth in an assembly of holy ones. This does not resolve the identity of every holy one.

source_unit.text: Hallelujah. Praise God among His holy ones; praise Him in the firmament of His power.

target_units.text: The heavens will acknowledge Thy wonders, Lord, and Thy truth in an assembly of holy ones.
